messages:
jordan: noticed a big jump in Prometheus scrape cardinality and remote_write queue backlog ~10m ago. p95/write_latency and pending_samples are spiking. remote_write logs show timeouts and 429s. any ideas?

alice: :eyes: can you paste the grafana panel? which cluster/namespace?

jordan: grafana dash -> https://grafana.local/d/Vg7l/prometheus-queue (sharing panel)
jordan: cluster: gpu-prod, namespace: monitoring, most affected targets: kube-state-metrics and node-exporter sidecars
jordan: logs snippet: ```time=\"2026-02-12T15:02:31Z\" level=warn ts=1707732151.123 msg=\"remote_write_request failed\" err=\"Post \\\"https://cortex.ops:9009/api/v1/push\\\": net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)\```"

ben: we rolled a labels-change DaemonSet yesterday that adds `pod_template_hash` and `instance` labels onto node-exporter targets. suspect explosion of unique label combos. saw similar pattern before.

carla: if that's the case, cardinality would blow up — kube-state-metrics + extra dynamic label = combinatorial growth. can we confirm by querying PromQL: `count(count by (job, pod)({__name__=~\"kube_.*\"}))` vs yesterday?

jordan: ran counts: today 18M series, yesterday 1.2M. yep that's the spike.

alice: immediate mitigation: drop the offending labels in scrape relabel_config for the affected job(s) and restart Prometheus config reload. also consider setting `honor_labels: false` if being overridden upstream.

carla: suggested relabel snippet to apply quickly (prometheus scrape_config):
```yaml
- job_name: node-exporter
  static_configs:
  - targets: ['10.0.1.23:9100']
  relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [\"__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_pod_template_hash\", \"__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_instance\"]
    action: labeldrop
    regex: \".*\"
```

ben: quick note — labeldrop with source_labels list is not valid; labeldrop takes regex only. use `action: replace` to set label to "" or explicitly `action: labelmap`? simplest: remove the labels by name with `action: labeldrop` and `regex: "(pod_template_hash|instance)"` targeting label names. example:
```yaml
- action: labeldrop
  regex: \"(pod_template_hash|instance)\"
```

jordan: applying labeldrop now to node-exporter and kube-state-metrics jobs, reloading config.
jordan: infra-bot: prometheus reload (config) triggered by jordan

infra-bot: config reload requested: prometheus-01 -> ok (timestamp 1900012399) :white_check_mark:

jordan: after reload, pending_samples dropped from 120k -> 8k, write timeouts reduced. still higher than baseline but moving.

alice: medium-term: update relabeling in Helm chart for exporters to avoid enriching targets with dynamic instance metadata. also add scrape relabel test to CI (small test that runs `promtool check config` + sample relabel dry-run).

carla: ops idea: add a recording rule to track cardinality growth per job to alert before it gets this bad: `record: job:series:count` -> `count({job=~\".*\"}) by (job)` and an alert if > threshold or growth rate > X per hour.

ben: also tuning remote_write queue helped: increased `max_samples_per_send` from 1000 -> 5000 and `batch_send_deadline` from 5s -> 15s, set `timeout: 30s`. that reduced backpressure spikes when cortex was slow. config snippet:
```yaml
remote_write:
- url: https://cortex.ops:9009/api/v1/push
  queue_config:
    max_shards: 4
    max_samples_per_send: 5000
    batch_send_deadline: 15s
  timeout: 30s
```

alice: awareness: pushing those queue changes helps but masks root cause; keep monitoring SLOs for remote_write and also watch Cortex ingestion latency.

jordan: noted. will open a follow-up runbook item to revert label enrichment patch and add a helm-level relabel to drop dynamic labels.

carla: fwiw, we should also tune alerts so we don't get paged for transient post-deploy blips; use a 5-10m for-for duration for pending_samples > X.

ben: created a short PR to helm: `charts/node-exporter#274` to remove instance label injection. linking: https://git.internal/reds/charts/node-exporter/pull/274

jordan: thanks all, monitoring panels look calmer. will keep thread updated if anything flares back up. :thumbsup:
